name: Ms. Qurrat Ul Ain Rehman
title: Founding Partner
description: Ms. Qurrat Ul Ain Rehman is a seasoned legal professional with over 11 years of advocacy and litigation experience, currently serving as Senior Partner at R & H Law Associates and Consultants. Her practice focuses on constitutional law, property law, family law, service law, corporate law, and immigration law, where she has successfully represented individuals and organizations in complex legal matters across diverse areas of law.

An LLM graduate in International Human Rights Law from Brunel University London, she brings a comparative and cross-jurisdictional perspective to her profile. Her advanced training includes International Human Rights Systems, Humanitarian Law, AI and Ethics, Islamic law, and Comparative Criminal Justice, allowing her to approach cases with both depth and innovation.

Her advocacy work is enriched by extensive research and legislative experience, developed through her roles at the Citizen Advice Bureau UK, Legal Aid Bureau, and Ministry of Law & Justice Pakistan. In these roles, she has worked on pro bono litigation, drafted legal instruments, and contributed to law reform initiatives aimed at strengthening access to justice and protecting vulnerable populations.

Alongside her legal practice, she has served as a Senior Lecturer and Cluster Head at Bahria University Islamabad, where she has supervised research on human rights, family law, and legislative reforms. This academic engagement strengthens her analytical and policy skills, informing her courtroom strategies with robust legal research and doctrinal insight.

She is also a Senior Editor at JURIST Legal News & Commentary, where she contributes to global legal discourse through analysis of contemporary legal developments. Her published work addresses pressing issues such as sexual trafficking, health rights, digital law, and regional human rights protection.
A member of the IUCN World Commission on Environmental Law, she actively engages in legal discussions around climate change, public interest litigation, and environmental justice.

Known for her client-centred advocacy, strategic litigation skills, and commitment to social justice, Ms. Rehman stands out as a legal professional who bridges practice, policy, and research with integrity and impact.

name: Ms. Hareem Hilal
title: Founding Partner
description: Ms. Hareem Hilal is a legally trained academic and legal consultant with a robust background in civil law and constitutional law, backed by over seven years of diverse professional experience across academia, government, and legal practice.

In her legal consultancy role, Ms. Hilal provides expert opinion and analysis on a broad range of regulatory, commercial, and administrative legal matters. She regularly advises on the drafting and review of legal instruments, including contracts, wills, and powers of attorney, ensuring compliance with statutory frameworks. Her consultation spans across various fields of law, including Company Law, Competition Law, Arbitration, Succession Law, Tax Law, and Immigration Law. In her litigation practice, she has drafted and pleaded civil cases before the district courts, handling matters related to specific relief, contractual disputes, and property rights, combining technical precision with strategic legal advocacy.

She has also worked in key public sector roles, notably as a Planning Officer at the Planning & Development Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where she supported the implementation of the Merged Areas Governance Project, conducted policy appraisals, and coordinated planning functions in development sectors. She has also served as a District Youth Officer, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where she contributed to youth empowerment through district-level programming aligned with government youth policy objectives.

Academically, she holds an LLM in Public International Law from the University of Oslo, with a research specialization in human rights and climate change. Her scholarly work has been published in both national and international journals, covering themes like regional human rights protection, sexual trafficking, and climate law comparisons between the EU and the US. She is also a member of the IUCN World Commission on Environmental Law (2021–2025) and a licensed Advocate of the High Court, contributing legal insight and strategic counsel to policy circles, development sectors, and legal institutions.

With a well-rounded mix of academic rigor, litigation practice, and legal consultancy, Ms. Hilal brings pragmatic, research-driven, and rights-conscious solutions to legal and policy challenges at both national and international levels.
